uwp_capture_status: ok: original UWP app launched (window 'Printing C# Sample', PID 54136) and its initial 'Basic' frame was captured as the golden reference (notes/uwp_golden_basic.png). Per-scenario navigation and per-control actuation of the UWP app could NOT be automated on this box: the UWP CoreWindow is hosted by ApplicationFrameHost and exposes an opaque UIA tree (only a Pane), and synthetic mouse input was non-functional in this session (SetCursorPos/mouse_event no-op). So the UWP behavioral baseline is limited to the visual golden of the initial page.
verdict_basis: Structural gate (83.3, pass=5/fail=1) reflects only the UIA tree, which is fully populated. Eyes-on visual judgment is decisive here: the migrated WinUI 3 app renders a COMPLETELY BLANK white window on every scenario (confirmed by two independent capture methods: window-bitmap and screen-region GDI). By the parity skill's own definitions, pass and partial both require a NON-BLANK screenshot; every WinUI scenario frame is blank, so each scenario is fail. Additionally the app crashes when Printing the Photos scenario, which also makes Disable Preview unreachable. User-visible fidelity to the UWP original is zero.
notes: The migration did real work (all 6 nav scenarios present in the UIA tree; Print handlers on Basic/Custom Options/Page Range fire and open the print experience; runtime status text is set). But none of it is visible to a user because the pages do not paint, and the Photos print path is fatal. A future skill fix that makes the pages render should move this score sharply upward.
